rationale: Round 1 built and passed correctness with no ICE fallback, so this round raises obfuscation pressure across the board: FLA is weighted as the primary control-flow transform (highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain, since a flattening dispatcher over fftbench's hot polynomial/FFT loops dramatically raises static analysis cost) with BCF pushed up as the second control-flow layer, accepting its higher RuntimeCost only at moderate weight so the dense numeric loops in fftbench/polynomial code don't suffer runaway slowdown; SUB and ICALL are kept high because arithmetic and call indirection obscure the benchmark's recognizable math primitives (FFT butterflies, CRC, Huffman tables) at low size cost; SPLIT stays enabled at modest gain as a cheap combinator with the other passes; IGV is raised for diversity since interleaving global variables hides data-flow structure across the 11 functions, with its moderate CorrectnessRisk (0.35) acceptable given two clean rounds; nothing is disabled since the previous candidate showed the pipeline tolerates full-pass application on this small (6287-byte text) binary, where size overhead from BCF/FLA matters little but runtime overhead in the benchmark's tight loops remains the binding constraint.
